subject.title: feat: Provider circuit breaker for quota exhaustion

question: Should OpenClaw add `quota_exhausted` as a new failover/auth-profile/plugin-facing reason with multi-hour disabled-provider semantics, or keep periodic quota errors in the existing `rate_limit` contract and tune cooldown policy instead?
rationale: The PR crosses provider routing, auth-profile state, plugin-visible hook behavior, protocol/schema surfaces, and documented failover semantics; code review can identify the missing propagation, but maintainer intent is needed for the permanent reason and hook contract.

options.title: Accept the new reason after full propagation
options.body: Merge only after `quota_exhausted` is added to all runtime/protocol/docs consumers, the branch is refreshed, and live or realistic exhausted-provider proof is supplied.

options.title: Keep the existing `rate_limit` contract
options.body: Close or replace this PR with a narrower cooldown/probe-policy change that avoids adding a new public/internal reason and hook surface.

options.title: Defer to a broader provider-health design
options.body: Pause this PR and fold the quota circuit-breaker idea into the broader provider bucket/key-pool and cron guardrail work.

recommendation.title: Accept the new reason after full propagation
recommendation.body: Merge only after `quota_exhausted` is added to all runtime/protocol/docs consumers, the branch is refreshed, and live or realistic exhausted-provider proof is supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent model fallback and auth-profile usage history makes this the closest routing owner for the provider failure semantics decision.
